AUTHORISES the Acting Chief Executive Officer to: 4.1 prepare a Staged Program Schedule of Works for the Floreat Kiosk refurbishment works; 4.2 advertise a Request for Tender for necessary trades and/or consultants; 4.3 appoint project trades or consultant(s); 4.4 proceeds with the detailed design and documentation, including associated infrastructure; 4.5 approve of a tender up to a value of $250,000 for this project (in liaison with the Mayor); 4.6 proceed in preparing a Development Application and submission to the Western Australian Planning Commission; and 4.7 in accordance with Section 3.58(2)(b) of the Local Government Act advertise a Request for Tender for the leasing of the Floreat Kiosk for an initial term for a period of between 5 and 10 years (as nominated by the Tenderer in the response to Tender document) plus a further 2 x 5 year options. 5. REQUESTS the Acting Chief Executive Officer to submit a further report for the Council's consideration by no later than June 2019: 5.1 detailing a project capital construction estimate (if required) to be listed for consideration in the 2019/2020 Draft Budget; 5.2 detailing a Project Implementation Indicative Timeline; and 6. REQUESTS the Acting Chief Executive Officer to submit a further report for Council's consideration in August/September 2019 on the outcome of the Request for Tender for the leasing of the Floreat Kiosk

votes.title: Approve change of use - shop to small bar
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Pinerua, seconded by Cr Pelczar

That in accordance with the provisions of Part 4 of the Town of Cambridge Town Planning Scheme No. 1, the Council APPROVES the application submitted by Dunross Group Pty Ltd for a change of use from 'shop' to 'small bar' (use not listed) at Lot 623 (No. 294) Cambridge Street, corner Nanson Street, Wembley as shown on the plans dated 7 May 2008 subject to:- (i) the maximum number of patrons permitted within the Small Bar not to exceed 90 patrons at any time; (ii) hours of operation are from 12:00pm to 10:00pm Sunday to Thursday and 12:00pm to 12:00am Friday and Saturday; (iii) no live, amplified music is to be played at the premises; (iv) food is to be available to patrons of the small bar at all times during trading hours; (v) the sale of liquor for consumption off site is not permitted; (vi) a Staff and Patron Travel Mode Management Plan is to be submitted and approved by the Town, which shall identify all modes of private and public travel available to staff and patrons, in order to limit car parking demand (including walking, cycling, bus, train, taxis and car pooling) and shall specify how those modes and services will be promoted to staff and patrons to encourage and facilitate the utilisation of those modes (including methods such as annotated menus/wine lists, leaflets, timetables, free taxi-calls, travel vouchers and loyalty reward discounts or other incentives). (vii) a detailed management plan is to be submitted to and approved by the Town prior to the issue of a Building Licence. The Plan is to include the following:- • Public Interests Assessment (as required by the Department of Racing, Gaming and Liquor in any Liquor Licensing Application); • Trading hours; • Patron Numbers; • Patron Control (including staff training); • Queue management; • Sale of alcohol (no shots, jugs or offered drink promotions to be served); • Type of entertainment; • Impact on nearby residents and other members of the community (such as noise and other impacts caused by patrons accessing and exiting the premises); • Noise management • Public safety; • Security • Car parking (signage etc); • Complaint and reporting procedures; and • Access to taxi rank, complimentary taxi calling service and public transport services. (viii) in lieu of the on-site parking shortfall, payment by the applicant of the full cost of the construction of 90 degree parking within the Nanson Street road reserve adjacent to the side boundary of the subject property; (ix) construction of a 1.8 metre high solid fence along the rear boundary (abutting Dargin Lane). Plans detailing the fence (including provision for appropriate sightlines at the intersection of the lane with Nanson Street) are to be provided and approved prior to the issue of a building licence.

Lost 4/5

votes.title: Commercial development - Cambridge Street, Wembley
votes.quote: That upon the applicant providing confirmation of a legal right of carriageway to the rear laneway to the satisfaction of the Director Development and Sustainability, in accordance with the provisions of Part 4 of the Town of Cambridge Town Planning Scheme No.1, the Council APPROVES the application submitted by Swanstate Nominees Pty Ltd for a commercial development comprising one shop and ten office tenancies at Lot 50 (No. 339) Cambridge Street, Wembley, subject to the following conditions:- (i) the provision of a right of carriage way or easement in gross over the rear 1.34 metre section of the property abutting the laneway as indicated on the approved plan; (ii) the construction of the rear 1.34 metre section of the property abutting the laneway to the satisfaction of the Town. Details are to be provided to the Town's Infrastructure Services for approval; (iii) vehicular parking, manoeuvring and circulation areas indicated on the approved plan being sealed and drained to the satisfaction of Town, the 28 parking spaces being marked out and maintained in good repair; (iv) the provision of a 3.0 metre by 3.0 metre truncation at the intersection of Cambridge Street and Jersey Street. This truncation is to be transferred, free of cost to the Crown prior to the issue of Titles; (v) the awnings being designed not to interfere with the light signals. Details are to be provided at building licence stage; (vi) all awnings are to achieve a minimum height of 2.7 metres above natural ground level; (vii) a Construction Management Plan being submitted detailing how the construction of the development will be managed in order to limit the impact on the surrounding area. The plan will need to ensure that adequate space is provided within the subject site for the parking of workers' vehicles. The construction management plan shall be submitted and approved by the town prior to the issue of a building licence; (viii) all commercial car parking bays being made available to staff and customers at all times during the business day; (ix) details of any signage on site being subject to a separate development application; (x) the preparation and implementation of a Bin/Waste Management Plan detailing the storage method and collection details prior to the issue of building licence to the satisfaction of the Town's Infrastructure Services.

votes.title: DV21.26 - Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road - Primary street fencing refusal
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack

That, in accordance with the provisions of Town Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for alterations to the primary street fencing and gate at Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road, City Beach as shown on the attached plans stamped received 5 February 2021, for the following reasons:

1. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 and 4 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as when approaching the property from a north or south direction along Chipping Road the fencing infill (fins) are not open in appearance. Therefore, the fencing infill fins do not allow adequate visual connection between the subject site and Chipping Road, and the design of the fencing infill does not contribute to the streetscape;

2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the depth and spacing of the fins do not result in the open nature of the City Beach precinct being preserved. The solid appearance of the fins therefore have an adverse impact on the local amenity; and

3. The approval of the proposal will establish a precedent which may be considered in future planning decisions, which could result in a significant impact on the Chipping Road streetscape, and as such, is not consistent with orderly and proper planning.

Motion put and CARRIED (8/1)

votes.title: Alterations and additions at Lot 1381 Kilkenny Road, Floreat
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, and the provisions of Local Law 43 - Buildings on Endowment Lands & Limekilns Estate, Council REFUSES BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY the application for alterations and additions to the existing single house at Lot 1381 (No. 19) Kilkenny Road, Floreat as shown on the attached plans stamped received 29 March 2021, for the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(b) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced street setback would not be respectful of the established streetscape character and amenity of the locality as the proposal will not reduce the impact of parking structures within traditional street setbacks; 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setbacks will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the location of the carport. This will result in an unacceptable bulk and visual dominance on the streetscape. It is considered other locations on the site would have a lesser impact. 4. If the proposal is approved it may set a perceived precedent for similar developments to occur within the street setbacks of neighbouring properties, which would have an adverse impact on the streetscape and existing character of the locality.

votes.title: Ocean Gardens Retirement Village - Amendments to Constitution 2009
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Langer, seconded by Cr Pinerua That approval be given for amendments, as detailed in the attachment as circulated, to be made to the Constitution of Ocean Gardens (Inc) to reflect: (i) A review of the Definitions to remove ambiguities and improve the clarity of the Constitution; (ii) Replacement of the Objects. The current objects are for a nursing home; the new constitution adopts Objects appropriate for a retirement village; (iii) A review of and amendment to the Powers to make them appropriate for the Association at this point in time and in the future; (iv) Replace the Board member elected by the residents by a third Board member to be appointed from the business community. Create a new position of Observer to allow residents to send an observer to Board meetings; (v) Abolish the positions of Deputy Board member; (vi) A general review of the language used and bring a number of provisions of the constitution into line with current practice; (vii) Audited accounts and an annual report to be prepared and a copy of each document provided to the CEO of the Town of Cambridge.

votes.quote: That:- (i) the following fees and charges be adopted for additional bins, non-rateable and rate exempt properties for the 2009/2010 financial year:- (a) General Waste Collection: Domestic collection of additional 240 litre general waste bin on a weekly basis - $250.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Commercial collection of additional 240 litre general waste bin on a weekly basis - $267.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Supply additional 240 litre bins - $65.00 plus GST; (b) Recyclable Collection: Domestic collection of additional 240 litre waste bins on a fortnightly basis at $91.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Exchange of 120 litre Recycle Bin for 240 litre Recycle Bin as a once off charge of $Nil; Supply additional 240 litre bins in excess of policy - $65.00 plus GST; (ii) Council approves expenditure of $305,000 to be funded from the Waste Management Reserve, for replacement of all 120 litre recycle bins (estimated at 4,341) with a yellow lidded 240 litre bin for recycling; (iii) a compulsory Waste Fee on general waste bins levied under the Health Act 1911 in accordance with policies 5.3.1, 5.3.2 and 5.3.3 be set at the following rates for the 2009/2010 financial year:- (a) 240 Litre Domestic Bin $70 per assessment; (b) 120 Litre Domestic Bin $10 per assessment; (iv) Council endorses engagement of a Waste Minimisation Officer to actively assist in management of waste within the Town; (v) a further report be presented assessing:- the requirement for a dedicated green waste collection including a review of the existing twice yearly verge collection service; options for setting of a Waste Fee for the 2010/2011 Budget. votes.title: Social gambling community leased premises and council owned facilities approval
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Carr, seconded by Cr Powell

That Council:- 1. NOTES the following: 1.1 Western Australian Deaf Recreation Association (WADRA) requested social gambling be permitted at the Lake Monger Recreation Club (Inc) (LMRC), to which approval was granted for a three (3) month trial period; 1.2 The three (3) month trial period ended on 6 August 2019, with no complaints received in relation to WADRA's social gambling activities at LMRC; 1.3 Internal legal opinion was sought on whether social gambling is permissible at LMRC or any other Town-leased property or Community Facility; 1.4 Town Leases and the Community Facility Asset Management Policy (CFAMP) currently do not permit gambling (including social), with both expressly prohibiting such activity; 1.5 Any such approval, will require a Council approved amendment to the CFAMP, together with an approved variation to the current Lease with LMRC; 2. and 7. subject to satisfactory advice from the Town's legal advisors, the Mayor and CEO be authorised to enter into the Participants Agreement (PA) and Financiers Side Deed if the Mindarie Regional Council chooses to award the tender that guarantees the Mindar ie Regional Council's ability to meet its obligations under the Waste Supply Agreement with the successful tenderer. votes.title: Interim Appointment and Engagement of Legal Representatives
votes.quote: Moved Cr Timmermanis, seconded Cr Bradley That:- (i) the Town engages Natalie Lincoln of Price Consulting to run a recruitment process to appoint an interim acting CEO for at least 3 months duration commencing on or about 11 June 2018; (ii) the Town authorises and appoints MDC Legal to act on behalf of the Town and to provide advice in relation to issues relating to the employment of CEO, [private individual — name withheld], and approves payment of the legal expenses associated with the engagement of MDC Legal by the Acting CEO; (iii) the Mayor be authorised pursuant to Regulation 9 of the Local Government (Rules of Conduct) Regulations 2007 by the Town to provide instructions to MDC Legal; (iv) the Town approves the payment of Hall & Wilcox invoice number 420035 for $33,831.05 relating to the legal advice provided in relation to the Investigation; (v) for the purposes of the Dispute Resolution process under clause 18 of the CEO Employment contract the Mayor be appointed as a delegate of the Town to participate on behalf of the Town in Steps 1 to 3 of the Dispute Resolution Process; (vi) the Town authorises Hall & Wilcox to provide the Town with legal advice regarding matters raised in relation to the Department of Local Government Inquiry, and retrospectively authorises the advice provided by Hall & Wilcox in relation to this matter and further approves payment of their associated legal expenses by the Acting CEO; (vii) the Town authorises Hall & Wilcox to brief Patricia Cahill SC to obtain legal advice as to whether the Town can authorise the Mayor under Regulation 9 of the Local Government (Rules of Conduct) Regulations 2007 to provide instructions on behalf of the Town to facilitate the engagement of lawyers to provide independent advice to the Town; (viii) in relation to payment of accounts under Regulation 9(1) of the Local Government (Rules of Conduct) Regulations, the Council adopts the following procedure, in accordance with Regulation 11 of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations: AUTHORISATION OF PAYMENTS a. The Member authorised with the specific task shall confirm delivery of the services. b. The Council shall approve payment of invoices submitted and confirmed by the authorised member; (ix) the Town approves the provision of Legal Advice in relation to the CEO by Hall and Wilcox from the 9 April 2018 to 15 May 2018. Carried 5/4 For: Mayor Shannon, Crs Bradley, Everett, McKerracher and Timmermanis Against: Crs Carr, McAllister, Nelson and Powell

votes.quote: Moved by Cr MacRae, seconded by Cr Steele That:- (i) the Town of Cambridge Local Law No 43 be repealed BY AN ABSOLUTE MAJORITY, with this repeal to be effective from the date of gazettal of Amendment No 3 to the Town of Cambridge Town Planning Scheme No 1; (ii) an amendment to Town Planning Scheme No 1, known as Amendment No 3, be initiated to:- (a) insert the following new clause in the Scheme Text following clause 20; 21. ENDOWMENT LANDS AND LIMEKILNS ESTATE PROVISIONS (1) On Residential zoned land located within the area shown as the Endowment Lands and Limekilns Estate area, no building roof with a pitch of more than 5 degrees shall be constructed with silver or other similar coloured metal sheeting. (2) Notwithstanding (1) above, one outbuilding may be constructed on a lot from such material provided that it is; (i) less than 10 square metres in area, (ii) less than 2.4 metres in height, (iii) located outside of the primary street, secondary street or side setback areas. votes.title: Alterations and Additions - Dunkeld Street, Floreat
votes.quote:
Moved by Mayor Shannon, seconded by Cr Haddon-Casey

That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for proposed alterations and additions and to the existing frontage at Lot 1140 (No. 3) Dunkeld Street, Floreat, as shown on the attached plans stamped received 19 November 2022, the 27 November 2022 & the 30th November the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(a) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1, as the carport addition and excavation works will be located within the 9m primary street setback area; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setback will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the increased bulk of the carport within the street setback area, and will not be aligned with the Desired Future Character of the Floreat precinct under Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape; and 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed impact of the reduced street boundary setback does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, and will have an adverse impact on the local amenity as the natural topography of the site is unable to be interpreted due to the development not maintaining the traditional street setback. 4. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced primary street setback would not be respectful of the established character of the Floreat precinct and amenity of the locality due to the visual dominance the carport structure located wholly within the front setback, will have on the established streetscape. 5. If the proposal is approved it may set a precedent for similar street setback incursions to nearby properties, which would alter the existing character of the locality.

4. the Town of Cambridge will supply processable material collected via the red lid bin, which is estimated to be 6,500 tonnes per annum to the tender as per the Council's resolution at its Ordinary Council Meeting of 25 October 2016; 5. in relation to the commitment o f tonnes as detailed in 4 above, and the three conditions imposed within the Council's resolution at its Ordinary Council Meeting of 25 October 2016, agree these conditions have been satisfactorily met as follows:- • The technology chosen achieved a diversion rate exceeding 90%. • Results in a facility gate fee of less than $160 per tonne. • The revised MRC gate fee applicable to members waste being fully disclosed and acceptable to the Town of Cambridge. 6. subject to a Waste Supply Agreement (WSA) being finalised in an acceptable form and the matter of any risk associated with the calorific value of the waste being delivered to the facility being resolved to its satisfaction, it is acknowledged that the Mindarie Regional Council may choose to award the tender; and 7. subject to satisfactory advice from the Town's legal advisors, the Mayor and CEO be authorised to enter into the Participants Agreement (PA) and Financiers Side Deed if the Mindarie Regional Council chooses to award the tender that guarantees the Mindar ie Regional Council's ability to meet its obligations under the Waste Supply Agreement with the successful tenderer. votes.title: Energy from Waste - Mindarie Regional Council endorsement
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Bradley, seconded by Cr King That:- 1. the decision of the MRC at its Special Council Meeting of 18 May 2017, including the nomination of Tenderer A and Tenderer B as the first and second preferred bidders for the Energy from Waste Tender respectively be noted; 2. the Energy from Waste technology (EfW) being proposed in the preferred bidders' submissions be endorsed; 3. pursuant to clause 5.1(a) of the Mindarie Regional Council Constitution (as amended 3 April 2017), it is confirmed that the Town of Cambridge provides its agreement for the orderly and efficient treatment and/or disposal of waste delivered to such buildings or places as are specified in the tender submission of the preferred bidder, if any, that is awarded the tender by the Mindarie Regional Council; 4. the Town of Cambridge will supply processable material collected via the red lid bin, which is estimated to be 6,500 tonnes per annum to the tender as per the Council's resolution at its Ordinary Council Meeting of 25 October 2016; 5. in relation to the commitment o f tonnes as detailed in 4 above, and the three conditions imposed within the Council's resolution at its Ordinary Council Meeting of 25 October 2016, agree these conditions have been satisfactorily met as follows:- • The technology chosen achieved a diversion rate exceeding 90%. • Results in a facility gate fee of less than $160 per tonne. • The revised MRC gate fee applicable to members waste being fully disclosed and acceptable to the Town of Cambridge. 6. subject to a Waste Supply Agreement (WSA) being finalised in an acceptable form and the matter of any risk associated with the calorific value of the waste being delivered to the facility being resolved to its satisfaction, it is acknowledged that the Mindarie Regional Council may choose to award the tender; and 7. subject to satisfactory advice from the Town's legal advisors, the Mayor and CEO be authorised to enter into the Participants Agreement (PA) and Financiers Side Deed if the Mindarie Regional Council chooses to award the tender that guarantees the Mindar ie Regional Council's ability to meet its obligations under the Waste Supply Agreement with the successful tenderer. Carried 6/2 For: Crs Bradley, Carr, King, MacRae, O'Connor and Powell Against: Mayor Shannon and Cr Timmermanis

votes.title: DV15.23 – Retrospective Approval Carport Door SAT Reconsideration
votes.quote: COUNCIL DECISION: That, pursuant to Section 31 (1) of the State Administrative Tribunal Act 2004 (WA), the State Administrative Tribunal be advised that Council is not prepared to reconsider its decision to refuse the retrospective application for a carport door, as shown on plans dated 27 June 2014, for the following reasons:- (i) the proposal does not satisfy the design principles of clause 5.2.1 -  Setback of Garages and Carports of the Residential Design Codes of Western Australia; (ii) the carport door detracts from the streetscape and appearance of the dwelling and obstructs views of the dwelling from the street and vice versa; (iii) should the carport door be approved it would set a precedent for carport doors in the area; (iv) the Council does not accept that the door provides adequate security given the open side to the carport and the open fencing and believes the argument of security is an attempt to circumvent the planning policy; (v) an alternative exists for the applicant to use the garage which backs onto the rear right of way.

votes.title: Cambridge Bowling Club sub-lease decline
votes.quote: Moved by Mayor Mack, seconded by Cr Le Page That Council: 1. DECLINES the requested sub-lease to Floorball Revolution. 2. NOTES that the interested parties, along with other community and sporting organisations interested in space within the Town, will be invited to participate in the community consultation to be undertaken as part of the planned Leisure Asset Master Plan project.

votes.title: Cambridge Bowling Club alternative sub-lease proposal
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Delmenico, seconded by Cr Mayes That Council: 1. NOTES the multi-signatory letter submitted and the deputations received advocating for the proposal, and RECOGNISES the strong community interest and advocacy expressed in support of Floorball, and acknowledges the value that active recreation and emerging sports bring to the Town; 2. DOES NOT approve the requested sub-lease as presented; 3. AUTHORISES the CEO to work directly with the Cambridge Bowling Club and/or Floorball Revolution to revisit the proposal and explore whether an alternative solution can be developed that balances the needs of the sport, the Club, and the wider community; 4. REQUESTS that any options developed through discussions between the CEO, Floorball Revolution, and/or the Cambridge Bowling Club be brought back to Council for consideration including any considerations related to: 1. Financial implications and agreed reinvestment of the lease funds 2. Timing and alignment with, the Leisure Assets Master Plan process 3. Consideration of the recently endorsed Floreat Precinct Structure Plan. 4. The context of significant competing demands on community facilities, including other recent community driven proposals;

votes.title: DV15.23 – Retrospective Approval Carport Door SAT Reconsideration
votes.quote: COUNCIL DECISION: That, pursuant to Section 31 (1) of the State Administrative Tribunal Act 2004 (WA), the State Administrative Tribunal be advised that Council is not prepared to reconsider its decision to refuse the retrospective application for a carport door, as shown on plans dated 27 June 2014, for the following reasons:- (i) the proposal does not satisfy the design principles of clause 5.2.1 -  Setback of Garages and Carports of the Residential Design Codes of Western Australia; (ii) the carport door detracts from the streetscape and appearance of the dwelling and obstructs views of the dwelling from the street and vice versa; (iii) should the carport door be approved it would set a precedent for carport doors in the area; (iv) the Council does not accept that the door provides adequate security given the open side to the carport and the open fencing and believes the argument of security is an attempt to circumvent the planning policy; (v) an alternative exists for the applicant to use the garage which backs onto the rear right of way.

votes.quote: COUNCIL DECISION: That, pursuant to Section 31 (1) of the State Administrative Tribunal Act 2004 (WA), the State Administrative Tribunal be advised that Council is not prepared to reconsider its decision to refuse the retrospective application for a carport door, as shown on plans dated 27 June 2014, for the following reasons:- (i) the proposal does not satisfy the design principles of clause 5.2.1 -  Setback of Garages and Carports of the Residential Design Codes of Western Australia; (ii) the carport door detracts from the streetscape and appearance of the dwelling and obstructs views of the dwelling from the street and vice versa; (iii) should the carport door be approved it would set a precedent for carport doors in the area; (iv) the Council does not accept that the door provides adequate security given the open side to the carport and the open fencing and believes the argument of security is an attempt to circumvent the planning policy; (v) an alternative exists for the applicant to use the garage which backs onto the rear right of way.

votes.title: Alterations and Additions - Dunkeld Street, Floreat
votes.quote:
Moved by Mayor Shannon, seconded by Cr Haddon-Casey

That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for proposed alterations and additions and to the existing frontage at Lot 1140 (No. 3) Dunkeld Street, Floreat, as shown on the attached plans stamped received 19 November 2022, the 27 November 2022 & the 30th November the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(a) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1, as the carport addition and excavation works will be located within the 9m primary street setback area; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setback will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the increased bulk of the carport within the street setback area, and will not be aligned with the Desired Future Character of the Floreat precinct under Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape; and 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed impact of the reduced street boundary setback does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, and will have an adverse impact on the local amenity as the natural topography of the site is unable to be interpreted due to the development not maintaining the traditional street setback. 4. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced primary street setback would not be respectful of the established character of the Floreat precinct and amenity of the locality due to the visual dominance the carport structure located wholly within the front setback, will have on the established streetscape. 5. If the proposal is approved it may set a precedent for similar street setback incursions to nearby properties, which would alter the existing character of the locality.

votes.title: DV21.26 - Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road - Primary street fencing refusal
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack

That, in accordance with the provisions of Town Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for alterations to the primary street fencing and gate at Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road, City Beach as shown on the attached plans stamped received 5 February 2021, for the following reasons:

1. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 and 4 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as when approaching the property from a north or south direction along Chipping Road the fencing infill (fins) are not open in appearance. Therefore, the fencing infill fins do not allow adequate visual connection between the subject site and Chipping Road, and the design of the fencing infill does not contribute to the streetscape;

2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the depth and spacing of the fins do not result in the open nature of the City Beach precinct being preserved. The solid appearance of the fins therefore have an adverse impact on the local amenity; and

3. The approval of the proposal will establish a precedent which may be considered in future planning decisions, which could result in a significant impact on the Chipping Road streetscape, and as such, is not consistent with orderly and proper planning.

Motion put and CARRIED (8/1)

votes.title: Alterations and additions at Lot 1381 Kilkenny Road, Floreat
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, and the provisions of Local Law 43 - Buildings on Endowment Lands & Limekilns Estate, Council REFUSES BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY the application for alterations and additions to the existing single house at Lot 1381 (No. 19) Kilkenny Road, Floreat as shown on the attached plans stamped received 29 March 2021, for the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(b) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced street setback would not be respectful of the established streetscape character and amenity of the locality as the proposal will not reduce the impact of parking structures within traditional street setbacks; 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setbacks will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the location of the carport. This will result in an unacceptable bulk and visual dominance on the streetscape. It is considered other locations on the site would have a lesser impact. 4. If the proposal is approved it may set a perceived precedent for similar developments to occur within the street setbacks of neighbouring properties, which would have an adverse impact on the streetscape and existing character of the locality.

votes.title: Ocean Gardens Retirement Village - Amendments to Constitution 2009
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Langer, seconded by Cr Pinerua That approval be given for amendments, as detailed in the attachment as circulated, to be made to the Constitution of Ocean Gardens (Inc) to reflect: (i) A review of the Definitions to remove ambiguities and improve the clarity of the Constitution; (ii) Replacement of the Objects. The current objects are for a nursing home; the new constitution adopts Objects appropriate for a retirement village; (iii) A review of and amendment to the Powers to make them appropriate for the Association at this point in time and in the future; (iv) Replace the Board member elected by the residents by a third Board member to be appointed from the business community. Create a new position of Observer to allow residents to send an observer to Board meetings; (v) Abolish the positions of Deputy Board member; (vi) A general review of the language used and bring a number of provisions of the constitution into line with current practice; (vii) Audited accounts and an annual report to be prepared and a copy of each document provided to the CEO of the Town of Cambridge.

votes.title: Waste Management Fees and Charges 2009/2010
votes.quote: That:- (i) the following fees and charges be adopted for additional bins, non-rateable and rate exempt properties for the 2009/2010 financial year:- (a) General Waste Collection: Domestic collection of additional 240 litre general waste bin on a weekly basis - $250.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Commercial collection of additional 240 litre general waste bin on a weekly basis - $267.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Supply additional 240 litre bins - $65.00 plus GST; (b) Recyclable Collection: Domestic collection of additional 240 litre waste bins on a fortnightly basis at $91.00 (inc GST) per bin per year; Exchange of 120 litre Recycle Bin for 240 litre Recycle Bin as a once off charge of $Nil; Supply additional 240 litre bins in excess of policy - $65.00 plus GST; (ii) Council approves expenditure of $305,000 to be funded from the Waste Management Reserve, for replacement of all 120 litre recycle bins (estimated at 4,341) with a yellow lidded 240 litre bin for recycling; (iii) a compulsory Waste Fee on general waste bins levied under the Health Act 1911 in accordance with policies 5.3.1, 5.3.2 and 5.3.3 be set at the following rates for the 2009/2010 financial year:- (a) 240 Litre Domestic Bin $70 per assessment; (b) 120 Litre Domestic Bin $10 per assessment; (iv) Council endorses engagement of a Waste Minimisation Officer to actively assist in management of waste within the Town; (v) a further report be presented assessing:- the requirement for a dedicated green waste collection including a review of the existing twice yearly verge collection service; options for setting of a Waste Fee for the 2010/2011 Budget. To include a split fee for 240 litre/120 litre bins and to include all collection, management and disposal costs; changes required to policies 5.3.1, 5.3.2 and 5.3.3.

votes.title: DV21.26 - Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road - Primary street fencing refusal
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack

That, in accordance with the provisions of Town Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for alterations to the primary street fencing and gate at Lot 148 (No. 62) Chipping Road, City Beach as shown on the attached plans stamped received 5 February 2021, for the following reasons:

1. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 and 4 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as when approaching the property from a north or south direction along Chipping Road the fencing infill (fins) are not open in appearance. Therefore, the fencing infill fins do not allow adequate visual connection between the subject site and Chipping Road, and the design of the fencing infill does not contribute to the streetscape;

2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the depth and spacing of the fins do not result in the open nature of the City Beach precinct being preserved. The solid appearance of the fins therefore have an adverse impact on the local amenity; and

3. The approval of the proposal will establish a precedent which may be considered in future planning decisions, which could result in a significant impact on the Chipping Road streetscape, and as such, is not consistent with orderly and proper planning.

Motion put and CARRIED (8/1)

votes.title: Patio addition at Lot 1649 Glengariff Drive, Floreat
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, and the provisions of Local Law 43 - Buildings on Endowment Lands & Limekilns Estate, Council APPROVES BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY the application for an alfresco at Lot 1649 (No. 93) Glengariff Drive, Floreat as shown on the attached plans stamped received 11 January 2021, subject to the following conditions: 1. The development shall at all times comply with the application and the approved plans, subject to any modifications required as a consequence of any conditions of this approval; 2. The support columns of the alfresco shall be set back at least 9m from the primary street, with a maximum eave overhang into the street setback area of 1m; and 3. All stormwater shall be contained and disposed of on-site for the life of the development to the satisfaction of the Town.

votes.title: Alterations and additions at Lot 1381 Kilkenny Road, Floreat
votes.quote: Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr Mack That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, and the provisions of Local Law 43 - Buildings on Endowment Lands & Limekilns Estate, Council REFUSES BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY the application for alterations and additions to the existing single house at Lot 1381 (No. 19) Kilkenny Road, Floreat as shown on the attached plans stamped received 29 March 2021, for the following reasons: 1. The proposal is a non-conforming application under Clause 26(1)(b) of Local Planning Scheme No. 1; 2. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 3 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the proposed reduced street setback would not be respectful of the established streetscape character and amenity of the locality as the proposal will not reduce the impact of parking structures within traditional street setbacks; 3. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed reduced street boundary setbacks will have an adverse impact on the local amenity due to the location of the carport. This will result in an unacceptable bulk and visual dominance on the streetscape. It is considered other locations on the site would have a lesser impact. 4. If the proposal is approved it may set a perceived precedent for similar developments to occur within the street setbacks of neighbouring properties, which would have an adverse impact on the streetscape and existing character of the locality.

votes.title: Lot 151 (No. 6) Maloney Way, City Beach - Proposed Boundary Fence
votes.quote:
Moved by Cr Everett, seconded by Cr McKerracher

That, in accordance with the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 1 and the authority delegated to the Town under the provisions of the Metropolitan Region Scheme, Council REFUSES the application for a proposed boundary fence abutting a Parks and Recreation reserve at Lot 151 (No. 6) Maloney Way, City Beach as shown on the plans stamped received 18 January 2021, for the following reasons:

1. The proposal does not satisfy Policy Objective 4 and 5 of the Town's Local Planning Policy 3.1 – Streetscape, as the solid fencing design will not allow visual connection between the subject site and the abutting reserve of Brompton Road. The solid fencing will also not maintain landscaped setbacks between the site and Brompton Road and will not contribute to the streetscape nor preserve the open nature of the area; and

2. The proposal does not satisfy Clause 67(m) and (n) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, as the proposed solid fencing will not preserve the open nature of the precinct, nor proposes a low or permeable design that is consistent character of the City Beach Planning Precinct. The solid appearance of the fencing will therefore have an adverse impact on the local amenity.
